subject: Proposal: regional failback window exemption — FinLedger
messages:
From: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@finledger.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@finledger.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short failback window for APAC→EU failover

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Following our exec review this morning, FinLedger is asking if we can agree to a narrower failback window when APAC triggers a cross-region failover into EU. Specifically, our compliance team is uncomfortable with the 6-hour failback window stated in the draft SLA for warm-standby failovers — they want that reduced to 2 hours for customer-facing endpoints tied to payment flows (roughly ~10% of traffic).

We understand this increases operational burden; to make it workable we are open to:
- an exception limited to payment endpoints (we can provide the exact endpoint list),
- guaranteed read-only mode during the window for non-critical services, and
- a higher severity escalation path with immediate paging.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a 2-hour failback for that subset, and if not, what compensating controls you can offer (e.g., faster warm-standby activation, pre-warmed slots, or an elevated SLA credit cap)?

Appreciate a quick response — legal wants the redlines in place before the next procurement milestone (EOW).

Thanks,
Marcus Hale
Head of Infrastructure
FinLedger

Attachments: none
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@finledger.com>, Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@finledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2029 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short failback window for APAC→EU failover

Marcus — thanks for the note and the clarity on scope. Short answer: we can offer a scoped exception with operational mitigations, but it requires documented compensating controls and an increased activation guarantee for the specified endpoints. Proposed approach below.

Proposal (summary):
- Scope: 2-hour failback window for up to 10% of customer-facing payment endpoints (customer to provide canonical list).
- Preconditions: a confirmed activation playbook (runbook), pre-warmed capacity reservation for the endpoints (reserved bursts), and automated traffic steering rules to minimize client impact during switchover.
- Mitigations: automatic KV-prefix caching for payment session tokens, priority routing through dedicated GPU pool during failback, and an on-call ops escalation (priority-0) for the first 12 hours post-failover.
- SLA economics: in exchange for the narrower window, Redwood requests a capped SLA credit for failback incidents tied to this carveout (propose 50% cap on otherwise-applicable credits) and a 12-month term commitment for the dedicated capacity reservation.

I attached a short matrix (activation_matrix.xlsx) that maps activities and ownership; also attaching a draft mark-up of the SLA deltas (FinLedger_SLA_Deltas_v1.pdf) for your legal team to review.

If that aligns, Marissa will loop in Legal to produce the formal redline; Jonas, can you confirm Ops is comfortable with the ES escalations and pre-warm requirements?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: activation_matrix.xlsx, FinLedger_SLA_Deltas_v1.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: regional failback window exemption — FinLedger

Kim / Jonas — quick internal note after reviewing Kimberly's proposal and the attachments.

- Legal: the 50% cap on SLA credits is acceptable as a starting point, but we need a hard definition of "failback incident" (time markers, triggering conditions) and a clause limiting the carveout to N named endpoints + tags so it doesn't expand over time. I'll prepare a redline by EOD tomorrow.
- Ops: the pre-warm and dedicated pool are feasible but will require a 48-hour lead time for ramping additional capacity for major releases. We should include a condition that the exception is invalid during platform-wide upgrades.
- CS: recommend a communications template for customers during the failback window to avoid support volume spikes.

Jonas — can you confirm the 48-hour lead time and whether on-call rotation changes are needed? If yes, we'll include a timeline for the runbook updates and an internal readiness checkpoint prior to contract signature.

Thanks — Marissa

Date: Sat, 13 Apr 2029 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: regional failback window exemption — FinLedger

Marcus / Samantha — following internal review, Redwood can accept the scoped 2-hour failback window for the named payment endpoints under the conditions Kimberly outlined and Marissa documented. Key acceptance points:

1) FinLedger to provide the canonical endpoint list and tagging convention within 72 hours of signature.
2) Redwood will provision the reserved burst capacity and update the runbook; ops lead will perform a readiness drill within 14 days of signature.
3) Exception is void during platform-wide upgrades or scheduled maintenance windows — Redwood will provide a 7-day notice for any such periods.
4) SLA credit cap of 50% for incidents attributable to the carved-out window; definition of incident and time markers included in the attached SLA delta document.

Next steps: Kimberly / Marissa will send a redline with legal language; Marcus, if that matches FinLedger's needs please countersign the DocuSign we uploaded here: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?s=ABCDEF123456. We will run the readiness drill and report results back to your team.

Look forward to finalizing.

— Jonas Weber
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
